content: Velpatasvir's pharmacokinetics can be influenced by hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. When co-administered with cenobamate, the dose of CYP2B6 substrates may need to be increased. Close monitoring is recommended. Chloramphenicol increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin significantly increases velpatasvir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Alternative therapies are recommended due to the potential for serious interactions. Similarly, clarithromycin increases voxilaprevir levels through the same mechanism, necessitating avoidance or substitution with an alternative drug. Cobicistat elevates velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Velpatasvir increases colchicine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. Co-administration with P-gp inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. If necessary, reduce colchicine dosage or frequency as per prescribing guidelines. Conivaptan increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cyclophosphamide increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but close monitoring is advised. Dabrafenib decreases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. Danazol increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but close monitoring is advised. Danicopan increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) transporters. Dose adjustments of BCRP substrates may be necessary. Monitor closely for toxicities. Darolutamide increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting BCRP. Co-administration with BCRP inhibitors should be avoided. If unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose reductions of BCRP substrate drugs. Drospirenone increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but close monitoring is advised. Velpatasvir increases duvelisib levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and BCRP transporters. Co-administration with BCRP inhibitors may increase duvelisib levels, necessitating close monitoring or alternative therapies. Efavirenz decreases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. Elagolix decreases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. It is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates closely and adjust therapy as needed. Enasidenib increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting OATP1B1, OATP1B3, and BCRP transporters. Co-administration with sensitive substrates of these transporters should be avoided due to the risk of serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce substrate dosages and monitor closely. Encorafenib increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and BCRP transporters. It also induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Monitor for increased exposure and consider dose adjustments of affected substrates. Enzalutamide decreases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. Etravirine decreases velpatasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. Fedratinib increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust doses of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary and monitor closely. Fexinidazole increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies due to the risk of adverse effects. Fluvoxamine increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Fosphenytoin decreases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. Fostamatinib increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and BCRP transporters. Monitor for toxicities and consider dose reductions of affected substrates. Fostemsavir increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting BCRP and OATP1B1/3 transporters. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies due to the risk of ALT elevations. Givosiran increases voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP1A2 substrates. If unavoidable, reduce substrate dosages and monitor closely. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and BCRP transporters. Monitor closely for increased plasma concentrations of affected substrates. Idelalisib increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Istradefylline increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider dose reductions of sensitive substrates and monitor closely. Itraconazole increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ivosidenib decreases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. If unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic efficacy. Larotrectinib increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but close monitoring is advised. Lasmiditan increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and BCRP transporters. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. Lemborexant decreases velpatasvir levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Monitor CYP2B6 substrates for adequate response and consider dose adjustments. Lenacapavir increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for adverse reactions and adjust therapy as needed. Leniolisib increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting BCRP, OATP1B1, and OATP1B3 transporters. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. Voxilaprevir increases levels of letermovir by inhibiting its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
